Absolutely—mentioning a personal project that showcases your hands‑on design skills, especially one that involves AI, can set you apart. Just frame it so it highlights the *design* work you did (user research, wireframing, UI polishing, iterative testing) and how it ties back to Monzo’s focus on customer‑centric, data‑driven product development.

**Key points to cover:**

| What to highlight | Why it matters to Monzo |
|-------------------|------------------------|
| The problem you solved (e.g., simplifying a common task) | Monzo values solutions that directly improve user experience. |
| Your design process (user personas, journey maps, low‑ and hi‑fidelity mockups, usability testing) | Shows you understand the full design cycle—exactly what Monzo expects a junior designer to do. |
| The “AI” element (e.g., recommending saving goals, predictive text, chatbot integration) | Demonstrates you’re comfortable applying emerging tech, a skill highly relevant to a fintech startup. |
| Results (metrics, user feedback, or growth in engagement) | Gives credibility and illustrates impact, even if it’s a side project. |
| Tools & tech stack (Figma, FigJam, maybe Python/JavaScript for the AI API) | Confirms you’re already fluent in the tools Monzo uses. |

**How to phrase it in your cover letter**

> “While working as a barista, I noticed I spent a lot of time juggling appointments and cash flow. I turned that observation into a side‑project: a *smart scheduling and budgeting* mobile app that uses a lightweight AI model to suggest optimal inventory restock times and personalized savings nudges. Building the app from scratch taught me how to translate data into empathy‑driven UI—from creating user personas and journey maps in Figma, to iterating on prototypes based on rapid user testing. The result was an app that reduced my weekly prep time by 30 % and earned a 4.8‑star rating on the internal beta test. I’m excited to bring this blend of self‑driven problem solving, an eye for detail, and a passion for data‑guided design to Monzo’s product team.”  

Feel free to tweak the wording so it matches your real experience, but keep the focus on *design*—the AI is a great hook, but the design story is what will convince them you’re ready for the role.
